Subject: Severe latency & 5xx spike — Reserved capacity not honoring target

Subject: RE: Severe latency & 5xx spike — Reserved capacity not honoring target

Quick ops readout —
- Root hit: we see KV-cache backlog on dedicated pool gpu-05 that PriorityOne is pinned to. During a short scheduling churn the pool lost a node (OOM-driven restart on one host) which caused adaptive-routing to spill requests into shared fallback paths; however, some routes for PO-3467 remained pinned and backed up in queue.
- Current impact: affected routes ~18% of their traffic; overall qps on their reserved set is ~40% of committed due to queueing and per-connection rate limiting.
- Suggested immediate actions (order matters):
  1) Reroute PriorityOne's failing routes to warm standby pool gpu-09 (capacity available) — this will reduce p95 within ~2–3 minutes but requires a short TTL flush of KV caches (we'll lose some session affinity).
  2) Enable BRST-42 burst for 30 minutes while we move & heal (estimated incremental cost ~$2.3k for the 30m window).
  3) Follow with a controlled canary back to gpu-05 once the host reprovision completes and KV cache warmup finished.

If Vivek approves the burst AND Ops confirms the reroute, we can send a short customer note with the mitigation plan and 30m ETA. I recommend offering a service credit framework in that note (we typically offer 5–10% of that window depending on impact).

I'll prepare the playbook steps for Ops and an outbound message draft for Jordan.

-marissa
